Article Title: IFF says govt order to GitHub on BitChat unconstitutional, demands its withdrawal
Article Text:
The app allows anonymous communication without mandatory user registration, phone number verification or centralised logging of messages

NEW DELHI: Digital rights advocacy group Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) has termed govt's order directing GitHub to remove the source code repositories of Bluetooth-based messaging app BitChat "unconstitutional and authoritarian".In a statement Friday, IFF said the order, issued by Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the home ministry, directed GitHub to disable access to three BitChat repositories, including the Android application and release files, within three hours. It added that the order warned the platform of loss of safe harbour protection and possible criminal prosecution for non-compliance.It argued govt relied on Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act and Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021, instead of the dedicated blocking framework under Section 69A of the IT Act and the Blocking Rules, 2009, that require procedural safeguards such as recorded reasons and an opportunity for hearing.IFF also contended that the order did not identify any specific unlawful content in the repositories and instead objected to BitChat's ability to function during internet shutdowns through Bluetooth mesh networking. It said anticipating potential misuse of a communications tool was not a sufficient legal basis for ordering its removal.The foundation criticised the three-hour compliance window, saying it effectively denied GitHub meaningful legal recourse, and demanded that govt withdraw the notice.
Article Summary: Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) has termed govt's order directing GitHub to remove the source code repositories of Bluetooth-based messaging app BitChat "unconstitutional and authoritarian" IFF said the order, issued by Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the home ministry, directed GitHub to disable access to three BitChat repositories.

Article Title: Boat launches Nirvana Eutopia 2 ANC with dual drivers and 80-hour battery, priced at Rs 4,999
Article Text:
Price and availability

Boat has expanded its flagship Nirvana lineup with the launch of the Nirvana Eutopia 2 ANC, a premium over‑ear headphone designed for users who move seamlessly between music, calls, gaming, travel and work. The new model brings together dual drivers, 45dB Adaptive Hybrid ANC, Hi‑Res Audio, 3D Spatial Audio and an impressive 80‑hour battery life, positioning it as a versatile all‑day companion. Boat says the Eutopia 2 ANC focuses on the features consumers rely on most — sound quality, noise cancellation, comfort, calling clarity and long battery life. “One device now needs to work across music, calls, travel, work and entertainment,” said Gaurav Nayyar, CEO, boAt.“With Nirvana Eutopia 2 ANC, we are building further in the premium segment with a product that is practical, high on performance and aligned with how people use audio devices today.”At the core of the Nirvana Eutopia 2 ANC is a dual‑driver setup engineered to deliver stronger bass, clearer vocals and better separation across tracks. The headphone’s 45dB Adaptive Hybrid ANC adjusts automatically to surrounding noise, keeping the listening experience consistent across commutes, cafés, flights and shared workspaces.For immersive entertainment, the device supports Hi‑Res Audio and 3D Spatial Audio, adding depth and width to music, movies and games. Battery life is another highlight — users get up to 80 hours of playback, and a 10‑minute fast charge delivers up to 12 hours of listening, making it ideal for long travel or workdays.Connectivity includes Bluetooth 5.4 and Google Fast Pair for quick pairing and stable connections. The headphones also integrate with the boAt Hearables App, allowing users to customise EQ settings, controls and listening preferences.Comfort features include Adaptive Fit, premium memory foam ear cushions and a foldable, swivel design for portability. For calls, AI ENx technology reduces ambient noise, while physical buttons offer easy access to playback, volume, voice assistants and ANC modes. The headphones ship with a premium hard carrying case.The boAt Nirvana Eutopia 2 ANC is available in Cosmic Black and Utopian White at a special launch price of Rs 4,999. It can be purchased via the official boAt website and leading e‑commerce platforms.

Article Title: FBI, NSA and CISA issue urgent warning: Iranian hackers hit critical US infrastructure and safety systems
Article Text:
FBI, NSA and CISA issued a joint warning

‘Tampering with safety alarms and emergency shutdowns’



Read the updated warning by FBI, NSA and CISA

The authoring agencies urgently warn U.S. organizations of ongoing Iranian-affiliated cyber targeting of internet-connected operational technology (OT) devices, including programmable logic controllers (PLCs). These actions disrupted PLCs across several U.S. critical infrastructure sectors through malicious project file interactions and manipulation of data on human machine interface (HMI) and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) displays, resulting in operational disruption and financial loss.

Last Update Description

This update adds new guidance on detecting malicious changes in reusable code modules exploited within Rockwell Automation PLC programs. It also expands scope to include observed targeting of

Schneider Electric

, Siemens, and potentially other branded/manufactured PLCs, emphasizing the importance of restricting direct internet access and providing best practices for secure deployment.

Affected Products

Potentially all internet exposed PLCs, including Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and other branded/manufactured PLCs.

Key Actions

Install PLCs consistent with manufacturers' guidelines and security best practices.



Remove PLCs from direct internet exposure via secure gateway and firewall; work with IT/OT team members and/or integrators to perform this action.



Query available logs for the provided indicators of compromise (IOCs) and check available logs for suspicious traffic on the ports associated with OT devices, including 44818, 2222, 102, and 502, especially traffic originating from foreign hosting providers.



For Rockwell Automation devices, place the physical mode switch on the controller into run position. If you suspect your organization was targeted, including against other branded PLC devices, contact the authoring agencies and PLC manufacturer for guidance.



US federal cyber agencies have issued an urgent joint warning, claiming that Iranian state-backed hackers are actively breaching and tampering with industrial control systems at US water and energy providers. In an updated security advisory, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the National Security Agency (NSA), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and the Department of Energy warned that “potentially all internet-exposed” industrial control systems across critical US infrastructure could be vulnerable to attack.According to federal investigators, the Iranian-backed hackers are targeting programmable logic controllers, which are the specialised digital computers that govern physical machinery, valves, and power switches across utility networks.As per the warning, by altering display data and programming logic, the attackers have forced systems into dangerous operational states without alerting human supervisors. CISA and partner agencies are calling on all critical infrastructure operators to immediately audit their operational technology, disconnect industrial control systems from the public internet, and enforce strict multi-factor authentication.
Article Summary: FBI, NSA and CISA issued a joint warning about Iranian state-backed hackers. Claimed that Iranian hackers are tampering with industrial control systems at US water and energy providers. Said that “potentially all internet-exposed” industrial control system across critical US infrastructure could be vulnerable to attack.

Article Title: Microsoft is quietly replacing OpenAI and Anthropic models inside GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook, and CEO Satya Nadella just explained the plan
Article Text:
Satya Nadella says Microsoft is now routing tasks inside GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook to its own MAI models whenever they match or beat frontier alternatives from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Why Microsoft built its own AI models instead of leaning on OpenAI and Anthropic

What reinforcement learning environments mean for Microsoft's enterprise customers

Microsoft has started routing work inside its own products away from OpenAI and Anthropic, and towards models it built itself. Satya Nadella laid out the reasoning in a long post on X, describing a system where Microsoft's in-house MAI models take over tasks once handled by frontier models from its partners. GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook are already showing what he called promising early results. Copilot Chat and PowerPoint are next in line.The logic is cost. Nadella's framing is that software now has a real marginal cost for the first time, which makes the choice of model a business decision rather than a technical default. Frontier models stay in the mix for frontier problems. Everything else gets pushed to something cheaper that performs just as well.Microsoft says its MAI models already beat general-purpose frontier models on many use cases while burning a fraction of the tokens.The MAI family arrived on June 2, when Mustafa Suleyman announced seven new models spanning reasoning, coding, image, voice and transcription. The flagship reasoning model, MAI-Thinking-1, was trained from scratch on what Microsoft calls clean, traceable data—no distillation from other labs.MAI-Code-1-Flash runs 5 billion active parameters and is built specifically for GitHub Copilot and VS Code. Microsoft claims it is comparable to Haiku but cheaper.That cheapness is the entire point. Microsoft's tuned model for Excel matches GPT 5.4 while running up to 10 times more efficiently, according to the company. At Microsoft's scale, across hundreds of millions of Office seats, that gap compounds fast.The mechanism Nadella keeps returning to is the reinforcement learning environment, or RLE. Rather than train a model in isolation and then bolt it onto a product, Microsoft trains models inside the actual product harness, rewarding them for finishing the tasks customers care about. Suleyman calls these training gyms. Microsoft is selling the same capability to enterprises through Foundry under the name Frontier Tuning, letting companies build models on their own workflow data.Nadella was careful about one detail. Models from OpenAI and Anthropic remain part of the orchestration system inside Microsoft products. He also set a test for whether Microsoft is genuinely in control: evaluation scores should keep improving even if any single model is pulled out. Memory, context, tools and skills sit outside the model deliberately, so no one vendor holds the leverage.For Microsoft, which has poured billions into OpenAI, that is a notable position to stake out publicly. The company is describing a template it expects other software firms to copy—use the expensive model where it earns its keep, and route the rest somewhere cheaper you own.
Article Summary: Microsoft has started routing work inside its own products away from OpenAI and Anthropic. Satya Nadella says Microsoft is now routing tasks inside GitHub Copilot, Excel and Outlook to its own MAI models. Microsoft is selling the same capability to enterprises under the name Frontier Tuning.

Article Title: Xbox now lets you stream games for free, if you sit through two minutes of ads first
Article Text:
Xbox is testing free, ad-supported cloud game streaming for Insiders—watch a two-minute ad block, then stream games you own for an hour.

What you can actually play during the Xbox ad-supported streaming test

Why Microsoft is testing free game streaming now

Microsoft has started testing an ad-supported version of Xbox Cloud Gaming, letting players stream games they already own without a Game Pass subscription. The test went live on Thursday, July 23, and it is open only to members of the Xbox Insider programme. In exchange for skipping the subscription fee, players watch a block of ads before the stream begins, then get a one-hour session with no interruptions in between.The ad block runs for roughly two minutes and plays before you join the streaming queue, according to reports citing Xbox sources. Once you are in, the game runs as normal—no mid-session breaks, no overlays. You do get countdown warnings at the 10-minute and five-minute marks so you can find a save point.Want to keep going after the hour? Watch another two-minute block and requeue.Only games you already own, plus free-to-play titles. Variety reported that the eligible list includes Forza Horizon 6 and 007 First Light on the owned side, and Call of Duty: Warzone, Genshin Impact and War Thunder on the free-to-play side. That is a narrower pool than the 1,800-odd titles Xbox Cloud Gaming supports overall.There is a reason this is landing now. Xbox console prices go up again on August 1—the Series X hits $799.99 and the 512GB Series S goes to $499.99—which is the third hike driven partly by the memory shortage.Microsoft has also announced 3,200 layoffs across its games group and is looking to offload four studios. Cloud streaming on a device you already own is a cheaper on-ramp, and Microsoft is openly pitching it at markets where consoles are expensive or hard to find.Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball framed the goal as giving players more affordable options and learning from how they use it. Microsoft published five principles for ads across Xbox, including a promise not to interrupt gameplay. Game Pass subscribers, who pay from $9.99 a month, keep ad-free streaming.
Article Summary: Xbox is testing ad-supported cloud game streaming for Insiders. Watch a two- minute ad block, then stream games you own for an hour. Only games you already own, plus free-to-play titles. Microsoft is openly pitching it at markets where consoles are expensive or hard to find.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Advocate booked for using AirDrop to steal pics of female lawyers in Kalyan court
Article Text:
The accused allegedly carried out the unauthorised transfers over several days by misleading women advocates into handing him their iPhones.

THANE: An advocate was booked after allegedly transferring private photographs and data from the iPhones of several female lawyers to his own device using Apple’s AirDrop feature at the Kalyan court premises.The accused allegedly carried out the unauthorised transfers over several days by misleading women advocates into handing him their iPhones.According to the complaint, he would ask to access their phones on the pretext of downloading court orders, and transfer personal files and photographs to his own device without their knowledge or consent.The alleged act came to light on Friday when one of the women advocates reportedly caught him in the act.Following the incident, several female lawyers confronted the accused on the court premises, and he was allegedly roughed up by the aggrieved advocates before being taken to the Mahatma Phule police station, where a formal complaint was lodged.Based on the complaint, police registered a case against the accused under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act, 2000.Investigators began examining his mobile phone and other digital evidence to determine the extent of the alleged data theft and ascertain whether more women advocates were similarly targeted. Further investigation is underway.

He would ask to access their phones on the pretext of downloading court orders, and transfer personal files and photographs to his own device without their knowledge or consent.

Article Title: Behind the bust: How Pune cops crack AI-driven Bishnoi gang extortion racket targeting bizmen
Article Text:
The Pune police crime branch cracked the cases after arresting three gang members and detaining a 17-year-old minor. (Representative Image)

TOI





PUNE: Criminals are silently mastering the art of using AI in their trade to have a digital edge over the sophisticated cyber police force.A mobile messaging app that leaves no digital footprint has made inroads into the underworld. Extortionists are thriving on a subscription-based call application. It routes normal calls through various servers.Pune police recently claimed to have unearthed a sophisticated Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered extortion network allegedly operated by the Lawrence Bishnoi gang members after investigating a series of ransom threats to four businessmen in the city over the past two weeks. They received extortion calls and messages demanding Rs2 crore to Rs50 crore.The Pune police crime branch cracked the cases after arresting three gang members and detaining a 17-year-old minor. The arrested accused have been identified as Pavan Prakashram Barad (24) and Satyaprakash Kaluram Shilora (25), both hailing from Hanumangarh in Rajasthan, and Ravikumar Rajendrakumar Jangda (33) from Sirsa in Haryana. The minor was detained from Bathinda in Punjab.The arrested trio worked in different industrial units in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad.They fired four bullets at a steel manufacturing unit at Mantwardi on Pune-Saswad road on June 18 after demanding Rs 50 crore in extortion from the unit’s owner.Three sophisticated foreign-made pistols and 10 cartridges were recovered from the trio in the net and the minor. Their cellphones were seized.Additional commissioner of police (crime) Tejaswi Satpute told“The suspects were found using a mobile messaging application that does not leave behind any digital trace of calls or messages. It was used to communicate among the gang members.”The investigation also revealed that the suspects relied heavily on technology to conceal identity and evade law enforcers. “They used a subscription-based calling application. It uses AI and routes normal calls through various servers across the globe before connecting them to their intended targets,” deputy commissioner of police (crime) Gauhar Hasan said.“Analysis of the seized cellphones showed that the gang members communicated among themselves through an encrypted messaging platform. They used the paid subscription-based calling application to contact their victims. This was done to evade surveillance by law enforcement agencies, particularly the police,” Hasan said.“The gang also exploited AI tools to generate and deliver threatening voice calls and messages, making it difficult for victims to identify the callers. The calls were made in Marathi though only a few of the accused knew the language. These appear to be AI-generated voice prompts that sounded like recorded messages,” Hasan said.Satpute said, “The investigation so far has revealed that Ravikumar, who worked in an industrial unit in Handewadi, was linked to Aarzoo Bishnoi and other members of the Bishnoi gang. He collected information on potential targets and shared it with Aarzoo and Shubham Lonkar.”Aarzoo is the brother of arrested gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. Lonkar is a Pune-based operator of Bishnoi gang. His whereabouts are not known after he was booked in Baba Siddiqui murder case.
Article Summary: Pune police recently claimed to have unearthed a sophisticated Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered extortion network allegedly operated by the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. They received extortion calls and messages demanding Rs2 crore to Rs50 crore. The Pune police crime branch cracked the cases after arresting three gang members and detaining a 17-year-old minor.

Article Title: Thrissur Pooram accident: Police moot mandatory safety training for fireworks handlers
Article Text:
HC has also recommended expanding criminal liability to include festival committees, organisations and other entities that place orders with manufacturers for excessive quantities of fireworks in violation of statutory safety norms

Kochi:

Poll Vote & Share your view Should festival committees be held responsible for fireworks-related accidents? Yes, they should be liable No, only manufacturers should be liable 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





A statement filed before high court by the Thrissur city police commissioner in connection with the major fireworks accident at Mundathicode in Thrissur on April 21 has recommended mandatory safety training and strict compliance with the Explosives Act and Explosives Rules.It has also recommended expanding criminal liability to include festival committees, organisations and other entities that place orders with manufacturers for excessive quantities of fireworks in violation of statutory safety norms. It suggested that temple committees and festival organising committees should be held jointly responsible and liable, in addition to the manufacturer and other persons responsible for the accident.The statement was filed in response to a suo motu case initiated by HC following the Mundathicode fireworks tragedy during preparations for the Thrissur Pooram fireworks display, which claimed 16 lives, injured several others and caused extensive property damage.The commissioner pointed out that most persons engaged in the manufacture and display of fireworks rely solely on practical experience and have not undergone any formal technical training in the safe handling of explosives.Similarly, many licence holders engaged in fireworks manufacturing are not adequately aware of the provisions of the Explosives Act and Explosives Rules.The statement further recommended periodic safety training and certification programmes for persons involved in the manufacture, storage, transportation and display of fireworks. It also suggested mandatory joint inspections by the concerned authorities before granting permission for fireworks displays, periodic safety audits, pre-event risk assessments and festival-season enforcement drives to detect illegal fireworks manufacturing units and unauthorised storage of explosives. The commissioner also recommended restricting entry to fireworks manufacturing units to authorised personnel to minimise the risk of accidents.The statement suggested making it mandatory to install copper grounding plates at the entrance of every fireworks manufacturing shed to safely discharge static electricity accumulated in the bodies of persons entering the work area. It also recommended that every manufacturing unit have adequate roads and open space around its sheds to facilitate the movement of emergency and fire rescue vehicles. Additionally, it suggested that each unit have multiple access points with independent access roads of sufficient width to allow the entry of large fire and rescue vehicle.
Article Summary: The statement was filed in response to a suo motu case initiated by HC following the Mundathicode fireworks tragedy during preparations for the Thrissur Pooram fireworks display. It has also recommended expanding criminal liability to include festival committees, organisations and other entities that place orders with manufacturers.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Faraday: 'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right' and how blind certainty is human nature's most dangerous trap
Article Text:
'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right'

"There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right,

The self-taught genius who questioned everything

The psychological trap of total conviction

Unyielding mindsets in everyday life

The virtue of staying open

A room full of clever people falls silent when someone speaks with total confidence. Doubt creates space for discussion, compromise, and checking the facts. Absolute certainty does the exact opposite. It shuts down debate, ignores warning signs, and treats any disagreement as a personal attack." warned the 19th-century scientist Michael Faraday.Faraday's observation cuts straight to a basic truth about human nature. The quote reminds us that total self-righteousness is far more dangerous than simple ignorance. Someone who knows they do not have all the answers will stop to look at new evidence. Someone who believes they hold the absolute truth feels no need to listen, check facts, or hold back.The origins of this quote belong to a scientist who spent his life fighting against easy assumptions. Born in 1791 to a poor blacksmith in London, Michael Faraday received very little basic schooling. He learned science while working as a bookbinder's apprentice, reading the pages he was hired to stitch together.Through hard work, he earned a job as an assistant to chemist Humphry Davy at the Royal Institution.Faraday went on to discover electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene.Despite his massive success in physics and chemistry, Faraday remained humble about human knowledge. He was a devoted member of the Sandemanian church, a small Christian group that emphasized humility and the limits of human wisdom. In his science talks during the 1840s and 1850s, Faraday often warned other researchers not to fall in love with their own ideas.While the exact words appear across different letters, journals, and accounts of his talks, Faraday regularly shared this main point: the most dangerous mind in a laboratory is one that has stopped doubting itself.Philosophers and psychologists have long studied why fixed certainty causes so much damage. In the 1990s, psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger published landmark research on human thinking, showing that people with limited knowledge in a subject often overestimate their own skill. This phenomenon, known as the Dunning-Kruger effect, shows that confidence often peaks before real understanding even begins.From a philosophical view, Faraday’s warning matches the ideas of Karl Popper, a 20th-century thinker. Popper argued that real science depends on testing ideas to see if they can be proven wrong. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.When a person loses the ability to accept that they might be mistaken, they stop using reason and start following blind belief. History shows that when absolute certainty combines with political, religious, or ideological power, the results are usually terrible. Strict regimes, historical trials, and sudden financial crashes all rely on leaders who are completely convinced of their own correctness.Today, Faraday's warning applies far beyond science labs. Modern digital platforms are built on tools that reward anger and extreme views over thoughtful debate. Online spaces often act as echo chambers, surrounding people with opinions that only confirm what they already believe.This creates leaders, managers, and public figures who refuse to change their minds when conditions shift. In business, major company failures usually trace back to bosses who were completely sure of their plans, ignoring early warnings and feedback from their workers. In health care, government policy, and personal life, a complete refusal to admit doubt stops learning and cuts off teamwork.In contrast, healthy teams depend on what modern workplace psychologists call psychological safety and intellectual humility. Groups perform much better when people can openly say "I do not know" or "I was wrong."Michael Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. When top scientists believed electricity and magnetism were completely separate, Faraday stayed curious, ran hundreds of failed experiments, and finally proved they were connected.Shortly before his death in 1867, Faraday wrote a letter about his desire to keep his mind free of rigid bias. He understood that knowledge is not a fixed wall, but an ongoing process of testing ideas against real-world facts.Holding onto a healthy sense of doubt is not a sign of weakness. It is a necessary tool for survival, keeping people open to new facts, better ideas, and the simple truth that none of us know everything.
Article Summary: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene. Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.

Article Title: Spain total solar eclipse 12 August 2026: Why thousands of eclipse chasers could miss the total solar eclipse

Why Spain's 12 August 2026 total solar eclipse will be different from most total eclipses



Why being in Spain's path of totality doesn't guarantee a clear eclipse view



Spain's total solar eclipse in 2026 begins a rare three-year eclipse series



Thousands of people are expected to travel to Spain on 12 August 2026 for one of Europe's most significant astronomical events in decades. The total solar eclipse will draw amateur astronomers, photographers and tourists from around the world, with many planning their trips years in advance. Yet reaching the path of totality alone may not guarantee the experience they expect. According to Streamline, the eclipse's unusual timing close to sunset creates a challenge that many visitors may underestimate. As the Sun sits exceptionally low above the horizon, even relatively small obstacles could block the view of totality entirely, making careful site selection just as important as travelling to the right region.Total solar eclipses often occur with the Sun positioned high enough in the sky to provide a wide choice of viewing locations. Spain's 2026 event is different because the Moon's shadow will cross the country late in the day, leaving the Sun close to the western horizon during totality.According to Streamline, the path of totality stretches across northern Spain and the Balearic Islands after beginning in northern Siberia and passing over Greenland and Iceland.As the eclipse progresses across Spain, the Sun gradually sinks lower, leaving observers with increasingly limited viewing angles. In western parts of the country, the eclipsed Sun remains slightly higher, but farther east it approaches the horizon, making clear sightlines essential.Being within the eclipse path does not automatically provide an unobstructed view. The position of the surrounding landscape becomes a decisive factor when the Sun is only a few degrees above the horizon.Reportedly, trees, low hills, nearby buildings and other features that would normally have little impact on eclipse viewing could completely block the Sun during totality. This is particularly important in eastern Spain, where the eclipse reaches its final stages just before sunset. A viewing site that appears suitable during the day may prove disappointing once the Sun drops lower.The report suggests that visitors should consider elevation and an open north-western horizon rather than simply choosing a destination inside the path of totality.Balearic Islands face the toughest viewing conditions for Spain's 2026 total solar eclipseThe Balearic Islands are expected to attract large numbers of eclipse visitors, but they also present some of the most demanding viewing conditions. Totality will occur only moments before the Sun disappears below the horizon, leaving almost no margin for error.As per the Streamline, authorities have introduced an Eclipse Horizon 2026 digital tool to help visitors assess local sightlines using topographical information. Some travellers are also opting for boat-based viewing locations in the Mediterranean to eliminate the risk of land-based obstructions.Weather remains another variable. Even if skies are generally clear, haze near the sea or a narrow layer of cloud close to the horizon could interfere with visibility during the brief period of totality.The August 2026 eclipse marks the beginning of an unusually active period for astronomical events in Spain.The country will experience another total solar eclipse on 2 August 2027 before hosting an annular solar eclipse in January 2028.This sequence has increased international interest in Spain as a destination for eclipse tourism while also generating strong demand for accommodation and local services in regions along the eclipse path. Rural communities expected to host large numbers of visitors have been preparing for the influx, with tourism linked to astronomy continuing to grow as a specialised travel sector.

Article Title: Google co-founder Sergey Brin turned his $450 million superyacht into a floating headquarters with an entire deck dedicated to work
Article Text:
A superyacht designed around work rather than leisure

Why Dragonfly's business deck stands out

Hybrid engineering beneath the luxury

Sergey Brin's return to Google's AI race

A billionaire who never seems to switch off

More than a luxury yacht

For many of the world's wealthiest people, a superyacht is the ultimate escape from work, offering privacy, luxury and a chance to disconnect. Google co-founder Sergey Brin, however, appears to have taken a very different approach. His 466-foot (142.1-metre) superyacht, Dragonfly, reportedly includes an entire deck dedicated to business, allowing him to continue working while cruising across the world's oceans. Built by the renowned German shipyard Lürssen and delivered in 2024, the vessel combines luxury with functionality, reflecting Brin's reputation as a hands-on entrepreneur who returned to Google's artificial intelligence efforts after the generative AI boom.Rather than being simply a lavish retreat, Dragonfly has effectively become a floating headquarters. Beyond its office facilities, Dragonfly reportedly features a helipad, swimming pool, spa, beach club and advanced security systems, blending corporate productivity with world-class comfort. The yacht reflects a growing trend among ultra-wealthy entrepreneurs to integrate workspaces into luxury vessels, enabling business operations from virtually anywhere.Dragonfly is among the largest private yachts ever built by German shipbuilder Lürssen. Measuring 466 feet (142.1 metres), it was delivered in 2024 and ranks among the company's biggest projects. The yacht was designed by renowned naval architect Germán Frers, while Italian design studio Nauta Design created its interiors and outdoor social spaces.Unlike most luxury yachts, where entire decks are reserved for guest cabins, spas or entertainment, Dragonfly reportedly devotes a substantial section of the vessel to productivity. Lürssen has confirmed that the yacht includes a dedicated business deck featuring a private office, a gym, a games room and a concealed helicopter hangar, making it one of the most unusual workspaces ever built at sea.The dedicated office is the defining feature of Dragonfly. Although Lürssen has not disclosed its exact dimensions, the workspace is believed to occupy a significant portion of the business deck. Industry observers estimate that the office, together with its surrounding facilities, represents a sizeable commitment to creating a functional workplace rather than simply another luxury lounge.The concealed helicopter hangar further supports this concept. Built inside the yacht's superstructure, it allows passengers to arrive or depart quickly without depending on ports or tenders. While detailed internal layouts have not been made public, the combination of a private office and aviation facilities reflects a design focused on convenience for an owner managing global business interests.Dragonfly is powered by Lürssen's advanced diesel-electric hybrid propulsion system. The setup combines diesel engines, controllable-pitch propellers, power take-in/power take-off (PTI/PTO) units and an electric azimuth pod drive to improve efficiency and operational flexibility during long-distance voyages.Hybrid propulsion can also reduce machinery noise and vibration when operating in electric mode, creating a quieter onboard environment. Although Lürssen has not specifically described this as an office feature, such engineering could provide a more comfortable setting for meetings, video calls and focused work while at sea.Brin stepped away from Alphabet's day-to-day management in 2019, but his involvement increased dramatically after the rapid rise of generative artificial intelligence. Reports indicate that he has worked closely with Google's engineering teams, contributing to AI development and helping accelerate the company's Gemini models.His work ethic attracted widespread attention in 2025 when an internal memo, first reported by The New York Times, described 60 hours per week as the "sweet spot of productivity". Brin also encouraged employees working on Google's AI projects to spend every weekday in the office, arguing that the race towards artificial general intelligence required exceptional commitment.Dragonfly appears to mirror Brin's personal philosophy towards work. Rather than separating business from leisure, the yacht integrates both into a single environment. The inclusion of a dedicated office, business facilities and advanced engineering suggests that productivity remained a central consideration throughout its design.Today, Brin remains one of the richest people in the world, with Forbes estimating his fortune at around $266 billion, although the figure changes with market movements. For someone overseeing investments, artificial intelligence initiatives and philanthropic projects, a conventional office may not always be enough. Dragonfly demonstrates how modern technology and luxury can merge to create a workplace capable of travelling anywhere in the world.Dragonfly is not simply another billionaire superyacht filled with lavish amenities. Its defining feature is the way it reimagines what a workplace can look like. By incorporating an entire business deck into one of the world's largest private yachts, the vessel reflects the changing lifestyles of technology entrepreneurs whose work rarely stops, regardless of where they are.While most people view the open sea as a place to disconnect, Brin's floating headquarters suggests that for some of Silicon Valley's biggest innovators, inspiration and business continue long after leaving the shore behind.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.

The yacht reflects a growing trend among ultra-wealthy entrepreneurs to integrate workspaces into luxury vessels.

Article Title: A UK village spent £35,000 building four beaver-style dams after homes flooded. It is now waiting for the next deluge during a hosepipe ban
Article Text:
Leaky dams, also known as logjams, allow water to flow through slowly instead of blocking it. (Representational AI image)

Customers have been asked to avoid using hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars, and filling paddling pools or hot tubs. (Representational AI photo)

From drought to floods

Beavers are called ecosystem engineers because they naturally reshape rivers and wetlands by building dams.

Learning from Beavers

East Anglia, a rural region in eastern England, is facing a hosepipe ban after becoming the driest part of the UK. But in one village in Norfolk, people are also preparing for the opposite problem of flooding.At Caistor St Edmund, the ground has become so dry and hard that it feels like walking on a paved road. Farmers have harvested this year's hay, but the crop is smaller than usual. If rain does not arrive soon, they fear there may not be a second harvest.The long spell of hot, dry weather has forced Anglian Water, a water recycling company, to bring in its first hosepipe ban in 10 years. People have been asked not to use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling paddling pools and hot tubs. However, they can still use watering cans.East Anglia is the driest region in the UK. According to Anglian Water, the area received only 39% of its normal rainfall this spring, making it the second driest spring on record. Many rivers are running at very low levels, reservoirs have less water than usual, and record-breaking temperatures have increased water use."Understandably, customers have wanted to stay cool and have fun in the sun, but the unrelenting conditions are placing the environment and water supplies under increasing strain," said Dr Geoff Darch, Anglian Water's head of strategic asset planning, as quoted by the BBC.He urged people to "hang up the hosepipe, let lawns go brown, cars go dirty and use water even more wisely".Today, people are being asked to save every drop of water. But residents of Caistor St Edmund have not forgotten what happened when there was too much of it.According to The Guardian, the dry weather is very different from what the village experienced in December 2020. Days of heavy rain overwhelmed drains as water rushed off nearby fields. Roads turned into fast-moving streams of muddy water, homes flooded despite sandbags, and volunteers worked to keep drains clear. Residents say it was the worst flooding they had seen.To reduce the risk of another flood, four wooden structures have now been built along Wash Lane, where the watercourse is currently dry. These structures are called leaky dams or logjams. They do not block the water completely, but slows it down. During heavy rain, they also trap branches and other natural materials, helping slow the flow before the water reaches roads and homes.Norfolk County Council has spent more than £35,000 on the project. The idea is inspired by beavers, often called ecosystem engineers because they naturally reshape rivers and wetlands by building dams.When beavers cut down trees and build dams, they slow the movement of water and create small ponds. These ponds also become breeding sites for wildlife such as dragonflies and amphibians, including frogs, toads and newts.Norfolk has a small number of released beavers, and some have bred successfully, but none live near this village. The wooden leaky dams are designed to copy the way beaver dams work and provide similar flood-control benefits.The project reflects a growing need to prepare for more extreme weather, with long dry spells followed by periods of heavy rain. While the leaky dams are expected to reduce flood risk, there are also plans for a large solar development in nearby fields. This could change rainwater runoff, the way rainwater moves across the ground before reaching streams and drains.
Article Summary: East Anglia, a rural region in eastern England, is facing a hosepipe ban after becoming the driest part of the UK. People have been asked not to use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling paddling pools or hot tubs. But in one village in Norfolk, people are also preparing for the opposite problem of flooding.

However, in 2022, there were some prospectors who, instead of looking at the shining shops, focused on an unexpected location: the cracks in the sidewalk.Using brushes, hooks, buckets and portable vacuum cleaners, the prospectors sifted dust and debris from pavements in and around the Manhattan jewellery district to recover traces of gold, platinum, diamonds and gemstones left behind by years of trading and jewellery repair. According to the International Gemological Institute , some street prospectors say they can earn hundreds of dollars a day, with some reporting earnings of about $300It entails collecting a mixed composition of soil, dust, metal shards, and other residues found in pavements' cracks and later separating them to search for any valuable contents. From reports on New York sidewalk prospecting, one example is Klesh, who began prospecting around the Diamond District at the corner of Fifth Avenue and West 47th Street.He uses a steel hook pick, brush, and vacuum to gather residues in pavement cracks and separates them to find heavy metals or gemstone shards. The residues collected through sidewalk prospecting are called "paydirt," a mining term for material that contains valuable mineral deposits.The Diamond District is one of the world’s best-known jewellery-trading areas. It includes hundreds of jewellery shops situated around West 47th Street, Fifth and Sixth Avenue in Manhattan, and it specializes in the trade of diamonds, gems, and precious metals.Because buying, selling, repairing and processing jewellery happen in such a compact area, small traces of valuable material can sometimes end up in street dust. Identification of the materials, however, is not always easy. According to the Gemological Institute of America (GIA), it is often hard to identify what kind of stone you have - a natural diamond, laboratory-made diamond, or a fake one. According to GIA, some special devices are often needed because sometimes diamonds cannot be recognised by just looking at them.There are many scientific concepts behind the extraction of metals from the soil, including gold extraction science. Gold is an element that has high density, making it possible to use its properties for separation using gravity separation techniques.According to the US Geological Survey , the dense nature and stability of gold cause it to deposit in certain places, and hence, it can be separated using gravity separation techniques from other materials of lower density. Street prospectors use the same principle but on a much smaller scale in order to find dense material from soil deposits.The hunt for useful and valuable items in urban settings does not stop at New York alone. Metal detecting, recycling and urban scavenging are practiced by people all around the globe in their search for useful and valuable objects.The distinctive feature of this activity is that ordinary urban dust may contain material linked to jewellery making. Although searching for diamonds and gold in the sidewalk cracks may seem like a treasure hunt, valuable materials are not so easy to recover.It takes patience, skill, and the capacity to find any valuable material amid the tons of waste. The Diamond District hunters' tale shows one of the peculiarities of city living, as amid millions of footprints and layers of urban dust, some valuable items may still remain unnoticed.
Article Summary: Prospectors in New York's Diamond District searched sidewalk cracks for valuable materials. They used brushes and vacuums to collect dust and debris from pavements. This residue, known as paydirt, contained traces of gold and diamonds. Valuables ended up on the sidewalk due to extensive jewelry trading and repair activities.

Article Title: America is committing trillions to rebuild. AI must help people build it
Article Text:
AI is useful, but only when it is grounded in the judgment of people

I have spent more than two decades building AI systems, and I am also a father of two young children. These two facts shape how I think about the future we are building. When AI companies claim they are building systems to replace people, I believe them. I know what this powerful technology can do, but as a parent, I worry about what we choose to do with it.The United States is entering a period of reindustrialization. Roughly $2 trillion is flowing into manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, semiconductors, and the industries that will define the future. But the people needed to build it are in short supply.What we build with AI, and who benefits from it, is still our choice. The numbers make the stakes plain. Manufacturing alone could face 2.1 million unfilled jobs by 2030, a shortage that could cost the U.S. economy up to $1 trillion that year. The construction and skilled trades sector is short more than 530,000 workers in 2026 alone. Aviation faces a projected shortage of 60,000 maintenance technicians by 2029 if the pipeline does not improve. And even as AI displaces some work in other sectors, 170 million new roles are projected to be created by 2030, roles that will require exactly the kind of skilled, experienced people we are struggling to find.The challenge isn’t simply finding more workers. It is helping people across the workforce build, share, and keep improving the know-how this moment demands. We do not have a shortage of know-how in this country, but every retirement takes decades of hard-earned know-how with it. For every five skilled workers who retire, only two enter the trades. That is the gap we should be asking AI to close.So, the question is not whether AI changes work. It will.The real question is whether we use AI to replace know-how or multiply it.Know-how earned from decades of work is different from written information. It is what people learn after years of doing real work: what to notice, when to slow down, when to escalate, when something feels off, and how to solve a problem that does not look like the textbook or the checklist.Think about a 22-year-old aviation safety mechanic on the first day of the job. Then comes a vibration, a temperature change, something that does not match what the manuals describe. An experienced mechanic may have seen that pattern before. They know when to slow down, when to escalate, and how to diagnose the problem.This need for experienced, embodied knowledge repeats across industries. An electrician wiring a new manufacturing plant. The construction supervisor who spots a problem before it becomes an accident. The manufacturing engineer who knows why a production line keeps failing. A nurse who notices a patient declining before the chart makes it obvious. The physician whose judgment helps treat complex cases. The small business owner who spent decades earning trust, training people, and learning how to serve a community.When that hard-earned know-how walks out the door, we all lose.Ford learned this the hard way. After three years of quality problems, the company turned back to about 350 veteran engineers and technical specialists to mentor younger workers, lead design reviews, and improve the AI tools used to catch defects earlier. Ford’s lesson was clear: AI is useful, but only when it is grounded in the judgment of people who know the work. Their expertise was not the cost to cut. It was the competitive advantage Ford could not afford to lose.Ford is not alone. Research shows that more than a third of companies that conducted AI-driven layoffs had to rehire more than half the workers they let go.Too much of today’s AI is designed to keep people coming back for answers, not to help them build lasting know-how. That is the same mistake social media made: engagement over agency. AI should not become another technology that takes human agency away. It should help people become more capable, not more dependent.What we need is AI that works alongside experienced people, continually learning from the decisions they make and the problems they solve, and helps bring the next person up to speed faster. In some roles, that could compress expertise that once took years to build into weeks or months of guided learning.That is one reason we started Cognisee: to build AI that learns with how people think, judge, and act, and puts that hard-earned judgment within reach of every person who comes after them, so we never have to choose between experience and scale.Building takes more than capital. It takes people who know how to build, fix, operate, and improve the systems our country depends on. And it takes making sure their know-how multiplies, not disappears.The promised age of abundance cannot be built by leaving people behind.The true measure of AI is not how much work it takes away from people. It is how much value it helps us create for families, businesses, communities, and nations.Because the future will not be built by AI alone. It will be built by people whose knowledge, judgment, and purpose are multiplied by it.
Article Summary: Manufacturing alone could face 2.1 million unfilled jobs by 2030, a shortage that could cost the U.S. economy up to $1 trillion that year. We do not have a shortage of know-how in this country, but every retirement takes decades of hard-earned know- how with it. For every five skilled workers who retire, only two enter the trades. That is the gap we should be asking AI to close.

Article Title: Deep beneath New Mexico, an isolated cave microbiome contains bacteria resistant to multiple antibiotics, suggesting resistance predates modern medicine
Article Text:
Lechuguilla Cave's isolated microbes show ancient antibiotic resistance mechanisms. These bacteria evolved defenses over millions of years underground. This discovery suggests resistance is an ancient survival strategy. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons

Secrets hidden beneath the desert rock

Understanding these natural defenses aids modern drug design. It offers a head start against future superbugs. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons

What ancient microbes tell us about modern medicine

Deep beneath Carlsbad Caverns National Park in New Mexico lies Lechuguilla Cave. Known as Lechuguilla Cave, this enormous labyrinth stretches hundreds of feet deep within the rocky Earth's crust, through dark passages and fragile crystal formations that have remained undisturbed for millions of years. According to the study Antibiotic Resistance Is Prevalent in an Isolated Cave Microbiome , for about four to seven million years, large sections of the cave have remained cut off from the outside world. There is no light here, no rainfall in its deepest chambers, and no evidence that people had previously entered this area.When microbiologists entered these sealed chambers to collect samples, they made a discovery that deepened scientists’ understanding of antibiotic resistance.The study suggests antibiotic resistance is not only a modern phenomenon driven by antibiotic use. Rather, it may be an ancient survival strategy that predates modern antibiotics.For the study, researchers sampled the cave’s microbiome, which had been isolated for over four million years. From more than 500 unique cultures, they randomly selected 93 bacterial strains to test. They found that some strains resisted 14 commercially available antibiotics, including daptomycin, and identified enzyme-based resistance to macrolides, along with a novel macrolide kinase and an inducible daptomycin hydrolase.To collect the bacteria, scientists targeted pristine, undisturbed chambers far from known entryways. They studied isolated chambers in Lechuguilla Cave with no signs of human presence, such as scuffs or footprints, indicating they were untouched by people. The chambers are sealed off, which likely limits outside contamination.When researchers screened 93 bacterial strains from the isolated cave against 26 distinct drugs, every single isolate proved resistant to at least one antibiotic class, with most showing resistance to multiple classes. Analysis of the Gram-positive bacteria revealed that, on average, roughly 70 per cent of the strains were resistant to three to four distinct classes of antibiotics. While some strains were resistant to last-resort drugs like daptomycin, they remained sensitive to synthetic drugs like ciprofloxacin and linezolid.Because these microbes were isolated millions of years ago, their resistance likely evolved long before the advent of modern human medicine. Instead, this resistance may have evolved through millions of years of competition underground. Nutrients in caves are extremely scarce, so microscopic organisms produce chemical compounds that inhibit competing microbes. To protect themselves from these natural compounds, nearby microorganisms develop molecular defences.This discovery fundamentally altered how scientists view drug resistance, indicating it is an ancient evolutionary trait rather than a purely modern crisis. Before this study, many clinical models treated antimicrobial resistance as a side effect driven largely by human medicine and agricultural overuse. While antibiotic overuse can promote resistance, the study found resistance mechanisms in the cave microbiome.The study also identified resistance mechanisms not previously documented in hospital settings. Some of the isolated bacteria inactivated antibiotics with enzymes that modified the drug molecules. Others produced proteins capable of breaking down synthetic drugs before they could take effect.Understanding these bacterial defences may help researchers study superbug resistance more effectively. Studying these defence mechanisms may help scientists anticipate how resistance could evolve. This knowledge may help pharmacologists design treatments that bacteria find harder to evade.By studying these ancient underground survivors, pharmacologists hope to uncover novel mechanisms of resistance today—giving medicine a head start in designing drugs that future superbugs cannot easily evade.
Article Summary: Study found bacteria in Lechuguilla Cave are resistant to at least one antibiotic class, with most showing resistance to multiple classes. These bacteria evolved defenses over millions of years underground. This discovery suggests resistance is an ancient survival strategy. Understanding these natural defenses aids modern drug design. It offers a head start against future superbugs.

Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Tech billionaire Mark Cuban has shared a bold prediction for the future of employment: as artificial intelligence (AI) changes traditional office workflows, companies will train incoming employees using immersive “job simulators. ” In a post on X on Thursday, former Shark Tank investor argued that traditional workplace onboarding, where junior employees gain judgment and domain knowledge by working with coworkers and hands-on experience, will soon be a thing of the past.To bridge the growing gap between entry-level hires and real-world experience, Cuban expects the “next great AI application” to be high-tech workplace simulation software.He compared the upcoming shift in corporate training to long-standing practices in aviation and motorsport.Commercial pilots routinely spend hundreds of hours in flight simulators to learn emergency protocols and flight mechanics safely on the ground.
